engine.name: .NET / XNA / FNA

Upstream records an in-game single-player example.
Multiplayer was not verified in that field note.
route: Start with a small tModLoader item mod in a new single-player world.

engine.name: .NET / MonoGame
engine.notes: SMAPI loads C# mods and supports a documented event API.

reasons: SMAPI is a maintained, game-specific mod framework.
Content packs can keep a first change small.
Use a separate farm to test save compatibility.
route: Use SMAPI; choose a content pack for data changes and C# only when needed.

engine.name: Java / Minecraft
engine.notes: Java Edition loaders are not interchangeable with Bedrock add-ons.

reasons: Fabric exposes documented hooks for Java Edition.
Upstream also records a NeoForge content example.
This entry covers a local single-player world only.
route: Choose Fabric or NeoForge for your exact Java Edition version; do not mix loaders.

engine.name: .NET / XNA / FNA
engine.notes: Everest is the community mod loader and API for Celeste.

reasons: Everest provides a dedicated modding API.
Custom levels make a focused first project.

engine.name: Creation Engine

reasons: Creation Engine plugins offer a documented content route.
Script extenders are version-specific and optional for simple edits.
A new test save helps isolate load-order problems.
route: Start with a small Creation Kit plugin; add SKSE only when your feature needs it.

engine.name: Creation Engine
engine.notes: The game runtime and F4SE release must match if you need native plugins.

reasons: Creation Kit plugins cover many content changes.
F4SE publishes compatibility for specific runtime builds.
A clean test save is needed before changing scripted content.
route: Use a small Creation Kit plugin first; keep F4SE optional.

engine.name: Gamebryo
engine.notes: New Vegas uses GECK-era plugins and xNVSE, not the newer Creation Kit.

reasons: xNVSE provides a game-specific scripting extension.
Small record edits can avoid native plugins.
Dependencies and save persistence need review.
route: Prefer a small GECK plugin; use xNVSE only for unsupported scripting needs.

engine.name: Creation Engine 2
engine.notes: Creation Kit content and SFSE native plugins have different requirements.

reasons: A Creation Engine content route exists.
SFSE supports specific game runtimes.
Check platform and extender support before planning code mods.
route: Begin with Creation Kit content; use a compatible SFSE build only if needed.

engine.name: Unity / C#
engine.notes: XML Defs cover data; Harmony is for more advanced behavior changes.

reasons: XML supports a small data-first mod.
C# and Harmony are available for deeper work.
DLC and load order affect compatibility.
route: Start with XML Defs in a separate mod folder and a disposable colony.

engine.name: Custom C++ / Lua API
engine.notes: Wube provides Lua prototype and runtime APIs; use documentation for your installed version.

reasons: The developer exposes a documented Lua mod API.
New recipes and items can use data-stage prototypes.
Expansion dependencies must be declared.

engine.name: Divinity Engine
engine.notes: Larian provides an official PC toolkit and in-game mod manager.

reasons: An official toolkit supports custom content.
Equipment is a focused first change.
Modded saves retain dependencies on installed mods.
route: Use the official Baldur's Gate 3 Toolkit for a local equipment mod.

engine.name: REDengine 4
engine.notes: Official modding support exists; advanced frameworks have their own compatibility requirements.

reasons: CD PROJEKT RED publishes modding resources.
REDmod offers a content-focused starting point.
Game updates can invalidate third-party frameworks.

engine.name: Unity / C#
engine.notes: Nautilus is the game-specific API; legacy and current game branches differ.

reasons: Nautilus provides Subnautica modding APIs.
A small item is easier to validate than a world overhaul.
Match the game branch before selecting dependencies.
route: Use the current Nautilus installation guide and a new local save.

engine.name: Unity / C#
engine.notes: The community Modding API is specific to Hollow Knight, not Silksong.

reasons: A dedicated community modding API exists.
The API avoids starting from raw engine hooks.
Game and API builds must be compatible.

The loader stack must match the current build.

engine.name: Unity / C#

reasons: R2API offers APIs for community mods.
Installed game, loader and module versions need checking.
Online sessions are outside this assessment.

engine.name: Unreal Engine

reasons: UE4SS documentation points to Palworld examples.
Engine versions and loader signatures can change.
Official servers and online play are excluded.

engine.name: Unreal Engine

reasons: WB Games provides an official Creator Kit.
The supported toolkit covers custom PC content.
Arbitrary code injection is not implied by toolkit support.
route: Use the official Creator Kit and in-game mod manager for supported content.

engine.notes: The upstream note examined a UE5.0 build; it reports a failed depth-compositing experiment.

Do not assume a GTA-style mashup transfers to this game.
route: Read the negative field note, then assess a much smaller supported local change.

engine.name: RE Engine

Loader compatibility depends on the game build.

engine.name: RAGE

GTA Online is protected by BattlEye.

engine.name: FromSoftware engine
engine.notes: The game includes online anti-cheat; an upstream offline experiment is not general approval.

Upstream offline research does not validate your installation.

engine.name: Custom / The Forge

Native loader support is sensitive to game updates.

engine.name: LÖVE / Lua

This site does not recommend client mods.
